traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.42, 0.13, 0.06], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leader.note: Imagekit woody-forms group 2 (2026-10-19, plantgen-claude project-files/image-data/woody-forms-2-2026-10-19/): leader lost in 13 of 25 photo votes, kept in 6 of 7 render votes.

traits.limb_course.note: Imagekit woody-forms group 2 (2026-10-19, plantgen-claude project-files/image-data/woody-forms-2-2026-10-19/TALLY.md): limb course wavy in 25 of 28 votes and limb habit tortuous in 9 of 23; Sargent (p. 799) does not describe their course.

traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 799): 'stout upright or spreading branches forming a narrow oblong or broad round-topped head'.

appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17), as Arbutus Menziesii: "slender branchlets light red, pea-green, or orange-colored and glabrous when they first appear ... becoming in their first winter bright reddish brown". Colour chosen by eye for bright reddish brown.

generator.params.bole_clear.note: Grown stems stand bare of branches for several metres below the crown in iNaturalist photographs (observations 263721768, 1914072): the crown from 5 m (crown_base), the stem forking at 4 m (fork_height), leaning and crooked (lean 20, wiggle 12, were 15 and 8), with fewer, bigger limbs (space_density 4, was 7).

traits.crown_form.note: iNaturalist research-grade photographs (observations 263721768, 1914072, 145154232): leaning, crooked red stems carry a rounded, irregular crown, clear of branches below.

traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 156 records annotated as flowering (Mar 4, Apr 79, May 72, Jun 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, April and May. FEIS (Arbutus menziesii) gives April and May on the Willamette, Mount Hood and Siuslaw National Forests of western Oregon.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Arbutus menziesii): ripe in October in the north of its range, the berry clusters staying on into December.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Arbutus menziesii chapter, text, read): minimum seed-bearing age 4 years (from root-crown sprouts), more commonly at least 8 years; FEIS repeats this, while the 1974 Seeds of Woody Plants (AH 450) gave 3 to 5 years.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Arbutus Menziesii: grows 3 m to 40 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Arbutus Menziesii: leaves 5 cm to 12 cm long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Sargent (1922), Arbutus Menziesii: petioles stout, grooved, about half an inch to an inch in length (the scan garbles the fractions; read as ½ to 1 inch, which the oak's, an inch at most, matches against Abrams' 15-25 mm), often slightly wing-margined toward the apex.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Arbutus menziesii (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.57 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 6 records in 5 sources); trunks 0.57, branches 0.54. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a broadleaf evergreen with a leaning, crooked trunk, an irregular crown, thick, glossy oval leaves and clusters of small white flowers. Not fitted to measurements. Its trunk is the pipe model's from its leaves, by the broadleaf trees' rules (2026-10-23). Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: USDA Forest Service Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005, public domain): its fitted age-to-dbh and dbh-to-height equations for coast live oak (Quercus agrifolia) in the Sacramento Valley region (Sacramento, CA; 60 open-grown park and street trees aged 2.4-134.5 years), since it has no madrones nor any tree of their family: the evergreen broadleaf tree that shares the madrone's California woodlands, from the city whose valley oaks stand for Oregon white oak, evaluated: 13.1 m and 51 cm at 30 years; 18.2 m and 80 cm at 50 years. Was 16 m and 40 cm at 50 years, from general knowledge.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: glossy dark green leaves; smooth, peeling orange-red bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: drooping panicles of pebbly berries about 1 cm across, still yellow-green, a few turning orange. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: white urn-shaped flowers in April and May; berries green in summer, orange-red from October, eaten into the winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): red-brown bark peeling in thin papery flakes from smooth greenish-tan inner bark; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves a little smaller than shade leaves; a young tree's leaves sharply toothed, an older tree's entire (juvenile until about 8 years); set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): white urn-shaped flowers 5 to 8 mm long, drawn as closed urns, opening from the base of each raceme up. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.opening.note: Days from the first flower of a cluster opening to its last: a third of the days from its first flower to its first fruit as they were set by hand before 2026-10-14, a convention (no source gives a raceme's opening time).

traits.flowering_position.note: FEIS's Arbutus menziesii review (page read): the flowers are borne in showy terminal clusters.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS's Arbutus menziesii review (page read): the fruit is a pea-sized berry of mealy pulp and numerous seeds, against the capsule most of the heath family bear.
